key_insight: Maestro improves Lean proof development by diagnosing failures and revising the global proof plan instead of repeatedly decomposing stuck lemmas.
engineering_relevance: Its coordination approach extends to verified code synthesis, where checked counterexamples trigger code repair.
method: Provers report why attempts failed, not just that they failed.
A coordinator uses the full proof context to guide provers, correct false lemmas, or retract and replan flawed subtrees.
Lean checks proofs; checked counterexamples send synthesized code back for repair.
evidence_signal: Across four frontier LLMs and ten benchmarks, the abstract reports gains over native agents on every unsaturated benchmark, including 34/48 versus 19/48 arXivLean theorems with Claude Opus 5.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify coordination overhead or compute budgets, leaving cost-adjusted gains unclear.
paper_title: Maestro: Agentic Formal Proof Development by Coordination
